title: Closed fill of a dry horizontal conduit, scored on cycle-averaged equilibrium (revision 2 of PV-TF1)
registrationStatus: PROPOSED, draft 2 (12 Nov 2026; draft 1 the same day; draft 2 answers the provisional verdict, reviews/verdict-r2-provisional-2026-11-12.md: approved for independent review only, not for registration or execution), after the technical review decision of 12 Nov 2026 (reviews/decision-post-run-2026-11-12.md). Not hashed, not registered, not run, not in spec/. Awaiting independent review. The original PV-TF1 registration (spec/PV-TF1.json) and run 1 (results/2026-11-12T15-00-21-588Z) are unchanged and are not superseded in place: this is a new experiment with its own identity
supersedesForFutureExecution: PV-TF1 (registered 12 Nov 2026): its instantaneous at-rest design is not executed again (decision of 12 Nov 2026). Its run 1 and statuses stand as recorded
process: a dry conduit filling from one end in a closed system, then oscillating freely in its natural seiche; storage at intermediate junctions and in the conduit, judged on cycle-averaged equilibrium
module: transient/pv-tf1-r2.mjs (not written; to be written only after approval)
relatedSpecs: PV-TF1 (its geometry, inflow, guards, hard validity conditions and sealing device are carried unchanged)
PV-C1 (its closure and level criteria are carried)
derivation: milestone2/pv-tf1-r2/DERIVATION.md (the mathematics, the error budget, every tolerance's justification); every derived number is computed by milestone2/pv-tf1-r2/derive.mjs into derived.json from the declared inputs only
equations: continuity of the closed system: after the inflow ends, the stored volume is constant, V(t) = V_in = 180.0 m^3 (no outflow: the sealing weir must never flow)

cycle-averaged books over a window w of length M T_ref (an integer number of reference periods): <V>_w = <A_t d_T1 + A_t d_T2>_w + <sum_s V_s(t)>_w + <sum_j NODE_VOLUME_j>_w, where V_s(t) is segment s's volume for a linear water surface between its two recorded end depths (references/volume.mjs conduitVolumeLinearSurface)

interpretation bound (DERIVATION.md section 3): |<V>_w - V_true| <= E_V,w = (1 + lambda) B_mean,w + lambda * max_t B(t) + C2,w, where B(t) = sum_s L_s |A(y_i(t)) - A(y_i+1(t))| is the monotone-surface bracket of the instantaneous surface (PV-C1's conduitVolumeBounds), B_mean,w is the bracket of the window-mean surface, C2,w = 0.5 |dW/dy| a_max,w^2 L is the second-order (curvature) bound, and lambda = (1 + eps) / (pi M) is the leakage factor of an oscillation of period <= T_ref (1 + eps) averaged over M T_ref
reference level: h_eq from 2 A_t h + L A_circle(h) = V_in (references/volume.mjs equilibriumDepth), 0.506637 m

reference periods (independent of SWMM): N = 1, the two-node lumped period 2 pi / sqrt(g A (1/S_1 + 1/S_2) / L) with S_i = A_t + W L / 2; N >= 4, the fundamental of the frictionless linearised lumped network that SWMM's dynamic-wave scheme represents (node area = tank area + half of each joined conduit's top width x length; link inertance L_s / (g A)), at h_eq
referenceAssumptions: R1' cycle-averaged still water: after the fill, the free motion is a superposition of the closed system's linear modes, every one of period <= T_ref (1 + eps) (true of the lumped linear network: T_ref is its longest period), with slowly varying (monotone over a window) amplitudes, about a mean state; checked by the period basis (W3), the linearity bound (W1) and the empirical leakage check (W4), not assumed
R2 the tanks are prismatic, 20 m^2, invert 0 (checked by the node-volume row)

R3' within each segment the water surface is monotone between its two end nodes (PV-C1's existing bracket assumption, references/volume.mjs conduitVolumeBounds); the books use the linear surface, the bracket bounds every monotone alternative
R4 junctions have zero plan area and zero volume; SWMM's junction volume is identically 0 (checked by a scored row)
R5 the declared inflow is the only source (reported row: the applied inflow against 180.0)

R6 the reference uses the declared inputs only; no SWMM quantity enters it. The bounds E_V, E_h and the uniformity threshold are computed from the recorded depths by fixed formulas declared here; they bound the interpretation of SWMM's state, they are not a reference value
boundaryConditions: unchanged from PV-TF1: the trapezoid hydrograph into T1, 0 -> 0.1 m^3/s over 60 s, held to 1800 s, to 0 over 60 s (180.0 m^3); the only outfall behind the sealing weir (crest 2.5 m)
geometry: unchanged from PV-TF1: T1, T2 prismatic 20 m^2, 3 m deep, invert 0; circular D 1.0 m, L 400 m, n 0.013, horizontal, zero offsets, N equal segments joined by N - 1 junctions at invert 0 (max depth 3 m); sealing weir W0 T2 -> OUT
hardValidityConditions: unchanged from PV-TF1 (V1-V4, including V3's reading of SWMM's nominal slope for a level conduit); any deviation invalidates the experiment

segments.unit: - (N = 1 a separate reference case; N = 4, 16, 32 the primary segmentation comparison, under the comparability rules of segmentationInterpretation)

durationS.unit: s (48 h; a design parameter, see DERIVATION.md section 7; not a criterion)

referencePeriodS.unit: s (derived.json; N = 1: two-node lumped period, N >= 4: lumped fundamental; all at h_eq)

scoredWindows.unit: - (K consecutive windows ending at the last routing step; the books and level are scored on the last, stationarity and drift across all three)

periodUncertainty.unit: - (eps, a-priori bound on |T_actual / T_ref - 1|: level tolerance 0.25 %, amplitude 1 %, time step < 0.002 %, friction < 0.005 %; sum 1.3 %, declared 1.5 %)

residualMotionShare.unit: - (beta: the share of each criterion that the interpretation bound may use, as in PV-TF1 draft 2's rest-flow derivation)

linearityFraction.unit: - of the hydraulic depth A/W at h_eq (0.399 m): amplitude bound a_lin = 3.99 mm

shiftedWindows.unit: - (empirical leakage check: windows of the same length shifted back by j T_ref / 8, j = 0..7)

headToleranceM.unit: m (SWMM's HEAD_TOLERANCE as registered; used only as the boundary between Qualified and Failed in the uniformity row, never as a reference)

solver: SWMM 5.2.4 production wasm through lib/swmm-run.mjs: CMS, DYNWAVE, EXTRAN, INERTIAL_DAMPING PARTIAL, MIN_SLOPE 0, MIN_SURFAREA 1.167, fixed 1 s, MAX_TRIALS 8, HEAD_TOLERANCE 0.0015; NORMAL_FLOW_LIMITED is the experimental factor (configurations). Production settings are not changed

PRIMARY.why: SWMM 5.2.4 accepts NONE (keywords.c line 70 -> NEITHER); dwflow.c line 255 then skips checkNormalFlow, the only routing use of the nominal WARNING 04 slope (F10). The segmentation comparison is made here

PAIRED.why: the registered PV-TF1 setting and production's (src/drainage.js line 409); scored with the same criteria, never pooled with PRIMARY; quantifies the limiter's effect on fill-time storage. NONE and BOTH are not assumed equivalent: each has its own validity conditions and rows

diagnosticsUnscored.what: PRIMARY with a 0.5 s step: time-discretisation sensitivity of the books
PRIMARY with MIN_SURFAREA 0.1 m^2: separates P2b (junction minimum surface area)
PRIMARY on the instrumented build: conduit volume (getter 420) as a decomposition only, after an exact equality check of every recorded value against production

configurations.matrix: 4 N x {PRIMARY, PAIRED} scored = 8 cases; 4 N x 3 diagnostics = 12 unscored runs; 20 runs in all. INERTIAL_DAMPING NONE (run 1's F2 diagnostic) is dropped: it does not bear on the storage mechanism

reference.periods: milestone2/pv-tf1-r2/derive.mjs (lumped eigenvalues by Jacobi; the continuum check kL + 2 atan(A_t k / W) = m pi)
reference.independence: the reference volume (180.0 m^3), level (h_eq) and periods (T_ref) come from the declared inputs alone; the tolerances are fixed formulas declared before any run; no run-1 number enters any of them

cycleAveragedEquilibrium.windows: K = 3 consecutive windows w1, w2, w3, each windowSteps routing steps, the last ending at the final step
cycleAveragedEquilibrium.averaged: every routing step in the window, unweighted (fixed step): tank depths and WSE, every junction's WSE and NODE_VOLUME, every segment's linear-surface volume, every segment's flow
cycleAveragedEquilibrium.amplitude: a_max,w = max over the window and over every node (tanks, junctions) of |WSE_i(t) - <WSE_tank-mean>_w|; also reported per node
validity: W1 linearity: a_max,w <= a_lin (3.99 mm) in every window
W2 interpretation bound: E_V,w3 <= beta * closureRel * V_in (0.018 m^3); E_h,w3 = lambda * a_max(T1, T2),w3 <= beta * equilibriumAbsM (0.2 mm)
W3 period basis: the mean of the zero up-crossing intervals of T1 - T2 over the K windows is within eps of T_ref
W4 empirical leakage: the spread (max - min) of <V> over the 8 shifted windows <= 2 E_V,w3
W5 level drift: |<h_tank>_wk - <h_tank>_wk-1| <= E_h,wk + E_h,wk-1 for k = 2, 3 (mean tank level stationary)
cycleAveragedEquilibrium.uniformity: U_w3 = max over junctions j of |<WSE_j>_w3 - <WSE_tank-mean>_w3|; tau_osc = lambda (a_max,j + a_max,tanks) + max_t v^2 / (2 g) (what a bounded oscillation can leave in a mean, plus the mean set-down of moving water)
classification: BOUNDED NATURAL OSCILLATION: W1-W5 hold, U <= tau_osc, books stationary: every row scored
IMBALANCE WITHIN SOLVER TOLERANCE: as above but tau_osc < U <= headToleranceM: uniformity row Qualified; level row Qualified; books scored (they do not assume a level surface)

PERSISTENT HYDRAULIC IMBALANCE: W1-W5 hold but U > headToleranceM: uniformity row Failed (numerical): SWMM's settled state is not level; level row Insufficient reference data (R1' not met); books still scored
CONTINUING DRIFT: W5 fails: level row Insufficient reference data; books scored only if their stationarity row passes
NOT RESOLVABLE: W1, W2, W3 or W4 fails: books and level rows Insufficient reference data (the oscillation is too large, nonlinear, or not the declared one, for the cycle average to be interpreted)

periodUncertaintyBudget.combinationRule: worst-case linear sum of the absolute component bounds (not root-sum-square), then rounded up to the next 0.5 %: 1.259 % -> 1.5 %

components.name: level
components.formula: max over h = h_eq +- equilibriumAbsM of |T1(h) - T1(h_eq)| / T1(h_eq), lumped model re-solved at each level

components.name: amplitude
components.kind: SCALING ESTIMATE, not a computed bound
components.formula: O(a / y_hyd) with coefficient taken as 1, a held to linFrac y_hyd by W1

components.name: timeDiscretisation
components.kind: SCALING ESTIMATE (phase error of a generic implicit one-step scheme; SWMM's iterated scheme is not analysed)
components.formula: (omega_1 dt)^2 / 12 for the fundamental (the leakage premise concerns the fundamental only: every other mode is shorter by construction)

components.name: friction
components.formula: zeta^2 / 2, zeta = (8 / 3 pi) (g n^2 / R^(4/3)) v_lin / (2 omega_1), v_lin the conduit velocity amplitude at a = a_lin

periodUncertaintyBudget.notCovered: model form: the difference between the lumped linear network and SWMM's discrete EXTRAN system (node-area definition, inertial damping at very low Froude number). Not bounded a priori; W3 is the run-time guard
leakageDependsOn: a monotone amplitude envelope within each window (not tested directly; a beating envelope is what W4 is meant to expose)
every mode period <= T_ref (1 + eps), true of the lumped model by construction

outputs: SCORED per case: cycle-averaged closure <V>_w3 against 180.0 m^3 (accounting; valid under W1-W4)
SCORED per case: cycle-mean tank level <h_tank>_w3 against h_eq (numerical; valid under W1-W5 and U <= headToleranceM)
SCORED per case (N >= 4): cycle-mean hydraulic uniformity U_w3 (numerical; Passed <= tau_osc, Qualified <= headToleranceM, else Failed; valid under W1-W4)
SCORED per case: post-fill book stationarity max_k |<V>_wk - <V>_wk-1| <= E_V,wk + E_V,wk-1 (accounting; valid under W1-W4)
SCORED per case (N >= 4): junction volume, every routing step (R4)
SCORED per case: sealing-weir flux, every step of the run, every step of the last window, and its integral (unchanged)
SCORED per case: tank node volume against A d, every step (unchanged)
VALIDITY per case: hard conditions V1-V4, stepping, G-node and G-link (unchanged), W1-W5 with their values

REPORTED, NOT SCORED: E_V and its two parts; a_max per node; the observed period; the shifted-window spread; mean segment flows; SWMM's continuity error; the applied inflow; the instantaneous books and every PV-TF1 rest condition (for comparison only, never scored here)

REPORTED, NOT SCORED: the paired limiter effect per N, Delta_N = <V>_BOTH - <V>_NONE with uncertainty E_V,BOTH + E_V,NONE; and the fill-phase limiter-condition counts under BOTH (as in the run-1 post-run analysis)
REPORTED, NOT SCORED: the primary segmentation comparison (segmentationInterpretation)
criteriaNotes: closureRel, equilibriumAbsM, sealFluxAbs, junctionVolumeAbsM3 and nodeVolumeRel are PV-C1's and PV-TF1's, unchanged. PV-TF1's instantaneous rest criteria (restWindowS, restLevelDiffM, restLevelDriftM, restSegmentFlowAbsM3s, restInternalWseAbsM) are not used for scoring here; they are reported for comparison. The cycle constants are design constants with a stated derivation each (DERIVATION.md section 5); none is chosen from a run. The uniformity, stationarity and drift thresholds are fixed formulas of the recorded state, declared here

segmentationInterpretation.N1: a separate reference case: a two-node system (no internal node) whose free motion is the two-node lumped mode (665.9 s), not the seiche; its books, level and limiter effect are reported on their own and never placed on an N trend
segmentationInterpretation.comparability: two segmentations are dynamically comparable for a mode when their lumped periods for that mode differ from the continuum's by at most 2 eps (3 %), the resolution of the period basis. A priori (derived.json): N = 16 and 32 are comparable in modes 1-3 (0.16/0.63/1.41 % and 0.04/0.16/0.35 %); N = 4 in the fundamental only (2.55 %; modes 2-3 differ by 10.6 % and 25.5 %); N = 1 in none (49.9 %)
rules: the N = 16 vs N = 32 difference is interpretable as a segmentation effect on storage
N = 4 is compared with them only for quantities governed by the fundamental (the cycle-averaged end state); fill-time differences involving N = 4 are reported, not attributed
no line, power law or extrapolation in N or 1/N is fitted; a direction ('rises', 'falls') is stated only where each successive difference exceeds the sum of the two cases' E_V
each case's W3 confirms at run time that its observed period is its own T_ref within eps; a case failing W3 leaves the comparison

predictions: P1 (open outfall explains T2-C): PRIMARY closes within the criterion at N = 4, 16, 32 (and at the N = 1 reference)
P2a (link storage carried by the end-node areas, J3): a closure offset of T2-C's sign, present at the N = 1 reference and at N = 4, smaller at 16 and 32, under PRIMARY

P2b (junction minimum surface area, J2): no offset at the N = 1 reference; an offset growing from N = 16 to N = 32 (and N = 4 below them), bounded by the J2 bound (1.8/8.9/18.3 m^3), and reduced in NONE-msa0.1
P3 (F1 excluded): the guards stay below 0.9 D (unchanged)
P4 (normal-flow limiter, F10): Delta_N exceeds its uncertainty at one or more N, with an N dependence; or no detectable difference within the stated uncertainty
none of P1-P4 is a pass condition; rows are scored only against the criteria
outcomeInterpretation: DERIVATION.md section 8 (table); every row is limited to this closed, horizontal, part-full configuration and to the end state; transientStatement applies
transientStatement: unchanged from PV-TF1: the closure in motion is diagnostic only; a cycle-averaged end state that closes does not establish that the transient was correct

failureClasses.accounting: cycle-averaged closure outside the criterion; book stationarity failed; junction volume not 0; sealing weir flow not 0
failureClasses.numerical: cycle-mean level outside the criterion; persistent hydraulic imbalance beyond the solver's head tolerance; books depending on the step beyond the criterion (dt0.5 diagnostic, reported)
failureClasses.invalidSetup: a hard validity condition, guard, stepping or sealing condition not met (unchanged)
failureClasses.insufficientReference: W1-W4 not met (books and level); W5 not met (level). Reported in three sub-classes, never merged

insufficientSubclasses.IR-motion: insufficient because the physical oscillation had not decayed enough: W1 or W2 fails while W3 and W4 hold
insufficientSubclasses.IR-basis: insufficient because the period or averaging assumptions failed: W3 or W4 fails (whatever W1, W2)
insufficientSubclasses.IR-drift: insufficient because the mean level was still moving: W5 fails (level row only)
insufficientSubclasses.distinctFrom: a Failed row (accounting or numerical) is a genuine storage, conservation or level violation with the reference valid

conservation: closed system: the declared inflow is the only source, the sealing weir the only possible sink
resolution: N = 1 (reference), 4, 16, 32; fixed 1 s step; diagnostic 0.5 s
assumptions: the API reads are SWMM's state at the end of each routing step; the final step is kept (PV-TF1 stepping)
limitations: the end state only; the transient is not scored
the interpretation bound E_V rests on R1' and R3'; W3 and W4 test R1' at run time, R3' is the bracket assumption accepted in milestone 1 (PV-C1)
the leakage factor bounds each modal component; a sum of modes is covered by W4 (empirical) rather than by a proof
J2 (minimum surface area) is not directly observable; it is attributed through the N trend and the msa0.1 diagnostic
the limiter effect is measured as an end-state difference; whether the limiter fired at a given step is not observable (no getter)
48 h is a design choice; if the bounds are not met by then the outcome is Insufficient reference data, and the duration is not changed after the fact
Manning friction at mm/s velocities is outside its range of validity (F11): the free decay is SWMM's, not necessarily water's; the cycle average does not depend on the decay law

W4 is a diagnostic, not a bound: shifts of T_ref/8 sample a mode of period T_m at phase steps of 45 deg x T_ref / T_m and are blind to a mode whose period divides T_ref/8 (at N = 32 mode 8 is close to that). Such short modes leak at most T_m/(pi W) of their amplitude, below lambda / 8

relationToFindings.F3: tested directly by P1, P2a, P2b; T2-C's registered rows stay Failed whatever the outcome
relationToFindings.F4: the in-motion volume problem is bounded, not removed: the cycle average cancels its first-order (oscillating) part and the bracket bounds the rest
relationToFindings.F10: removed from the primary comparison by NONE; measured by the PAIRED configuration (P4)
relationToFindings.F11: the oscillation is accepted as natural; it is averaged over its own independently computed period instead of waited out
relationToFindings.PV-TF1 run 1: unchanged; see DERIVATION.md section 9 for what carries over

validRange: a horizontal circular conduit filled from dry to below 0.9 D, closed system, ends at prismatic storage, free oscillation of amplitude <= 1 % of the hydraulic depth
scoring: automated, per case; PRIMARY and PAIRED tallied separately; status counts by error type; never a single pass percentage

proposedCriteriaHistory.why: first proposal of revision 2; not hashed
definition and reporting changes only: eps budget made auditable, Insufficient sub-classes, hybrid raw output, separate limiter arms, W4 limitation

rawOutput.everyStepChecks: all validity, guard, seal and stepping checks evaluated at every step for the full 48 h; all-step summaries kept
fullResolutionKept: every routing step of the K scored windows plus the 8 shifted windows (the last 3 M T_ref + T_ref)
the raw interval around any guard or validity trip, +- one T_ref
the complete configuration, generated .inp files and hashes
rawOutput.fullRecord: every step for the whole run archived outside git with SHA256SUMS committed, if practical
rawOutput.rule: the scored windows are never decimated

findingsRegisterRule: the PRIMARY (NONE) and PAIRED (BOTH) arms are reported as separate findings, never pooled: NONE answers the storage question without the normal-flow limiter, BOTH whether production's limiter changes it. A difference within the combined uncertainty is recorded as no detectable difference under this experiment, not as no effect
